<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 28"
    pfs=""
>
[Philosopher's Extractor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3122)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 301 <sup>2.0</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 8
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bizarre machine is a complex arrangement of flasks, tubes, and other alchemical equipment. The _philosopher's extractor_ is designed to create the ultimate alchemical concoctions. The extractor functions as an [exceptional alchemist's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702), granting a +4 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks related to alchemy.  When using the extractor to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an alchemical item or with [infused reagents](/Classes.aspx?ID=1) as part of your daily preparations, you can create impeccable alchemical items. An impeccable alchemical item always uses the maximum numerical value possible for any rolls it requires, such as dealing maximum damage with [alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75) or restoring the maximum number of Hit Points with an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91). If the impeccable item has a duration, it lasts twice as long as normal. Finally, an impeccable alchemical item never has a drawback.

**Activate—Accelerated Synthesis** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You use the extractor to produce an alchemical item of your level or lower whose formula you know. The extractor can create 56 levels' worth of items per day in this way. For example, the extractor could create two true elixirs of life (19th level) and two moderate elixirs of life (9th level), or eight [comprehension elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88) (7th level), and so on.

**Activate—Essence Transmogrification** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (manipulate)    **Effect** You take a sizable portion of a creature (at least two-thirds of its original mass) and filter it through the mechanisms of the extractor. After the end of the process, the _philosopher's extractor_ creates a transmogrifying mutagen that imparts the essence of the creature to the drinker. The extractor can make several transmogrifying mutagens simultaneously using the same activation if enough mass is provided at once, up to a maximum of 10 concurrent mutagens. Drinking a transmogrifying mutagen imparts you with one of the creature's unique abilities for 1 hour. This could grant one of several abilities such as a dragon's breath, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), flight, [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17), or immunity to [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145). The ability functions as it did for the original creature, except it uses your class DC or your spell DC (whichever is higher) instead of the creature's DC. The mutagen grants only abilities based on a creature's physiology and never grants magic-related abilities such as innate spells or spellcasting ability. The GM ultimately decides what ability a transmogrifying mutagen grants.

 Unlike normal for [mutagens](/Traits.aspx?ID=116) and [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effects, you can drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens and gain benefits from each. When you drink transmogrifying mutagens made from different creatures, you receive abilities from each creature. When you drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens made from the same type of creature, such as multiple mutagens made from trolls, you gain an additional ability for each transmogrifying mutagen you drink, and the duration of the abilities from that creature type increases by 1 hour for each additional concoction you drink.

 However, these additional benefits come with a risk; if you drink a transmogrifying mutagen while at least one other is active, after drinking it, you must succeed at a flat check with a DC equal to the total number of active transmogrifying mutagens you've consumed. On a failure, you fully transform into a member of the species of the latest transmogrifying mutagen you drank, and you almost always go berserk from your change. The transformation may leave some amount of your personality and memories intact, at the GM's discretion.

**Destruction** Simultaneously feeding the _philosopher's extractor_ sizable portions of an [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=2), [angel](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=3), [archon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=9), [azata](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=10), [daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=26), [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), [protean](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=82), and [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83), each of at least 14th level, along with a [philosopher's stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=133) causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Philosopher's Extractor

When using the extractor to Craft an alchemical item or with infused reagents as part of your daily preparations, you can create impeccable alchemical items. An impeccable alchemical item always uses the maximum numerical value possible for any rolls it requires, such as dealing maximum damage with alchemist's fire or restoring the maximum number of Hit Points with an elixir of life. If the impeccable item has a duration, it lasts twice as long as normal. Finally, an impeccable alchemical item never has a drawback. Activate—Accelerated Synthesis Three Actions (manipulate) Frequency once per minute; Effect You use the extractor to produce an alchemical item of your level or lower whose formula you know. The extractor can create 56 levels' worth of items per day in this way. For example, the extractor could create two true elixirs of life (19th level) and two moderate elixirs of life (9th level), or eight comprehension elixirs (7th level), and so on. Activate—Essence Transmogrification 1 hour (manipulate) Effect You take a sizable portion of a creature (at least two-thirds of its original mass) and filter it through the mechanisms of the extractor. After the end of the process, the philosopher's extractor creates a transmogrifying mutagen that imparts the essence of the creature to the drinker. The extractor can make several transmogrifying mutagens simultaneously using the same activation if enough mass is provided at once, up to a maximum of 10 concurrent mutagens. Drinking a transmogrifying mutagen imparts you with one of the creature's unique abilities for 1 hour. This could grant one of several abilities such as a dragon's breath, darkvision, flight, frightful presence, or immunity to sleep. The ability functions as it did for the original creature, except it uses your class DC or your spell DC (whichever is higher) instead of the creature's DC. The mutagen grants only abilities based on a creature's physiology and never grants magic-related abilities such as innate spells or spellcasting ability. The GM ultimately decides what ability a transmogrifying mutagen grants. Unlike normal for mutagens and polymorph effects, you can drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens and gain benefits from each. When you drink transmogrifying mutagens made from different creatures, you receive abilities from each creature. When you drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens made from the same type of creature, such as multiple mutagens made from trolls, you gain an additional ability for each transmogrifying mutagen you drink, and the duration of the abilities from that creature type increases by 1 hour for each additional concoction you drink. However, these additional benefits come with a risk; if you drink a transmogrifying mutagen while at least one other is active, after drinking it, you must succeed at a flat check with a DC equal to the total number of active transmogrifying mutagens you've consumed. On a failure, you fully transform into a member of the species of the latest transmogrifying mutagen you drank, and you almost always go berserk from your change. The transformation may leave some amount of your personality and memories intact, at the GM's discretion. Destruction Simultaneously feeding the philosopher's extractor sizable portions of an aeon, angel, archon, azata, daemon, demon, devil, protean, and psychopomp, each of at least 14th level, along with a philosopher's stone causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

This 6-foot-long scarf shimmers with the silvery light of the River of Souls while worn, providing illumination equivalent to that of a candle. You can deactivate or activate this radiance as an Interact action. The dangling lengths of a _ghost scarf_ softly billow in the presence of haunts, granting the wearer a +1 item bonus to all Perception checks and Perception DCs to resolve discovering a haunt or rolling initiative when a haunt triggers.

If the weapon already bears a _ghost touch_ rune, you instead gain a +1 item bonus to Fortitude saves against effects from incorporeal undead for 5 minutes.

---

The flower that adorns this hairpin is a blooming lotus flower that varies in color; it regrows in a day after the item is activated. Whether or not the hairpin's flower is in bloom, as long as you wear it and it's invested, it grants a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pluck the flower from the hairpin and scatter the petals, creating a flurry of color in a 10-foot burst centered on you. You become concealed for 1 minute or until you move from your current location. Any creature within the 10-foot burst when you Activate the Item must succeed at a DC 23 Reflex save or become [dazzled ](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) until the end of its next turn (or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) until the end of its next turn on a critical failure). The flower blooms again the next day.

---

The soles of these plain leather boots look like coils of flattened roots. The boots allow for full-foot flexibility despite their sturdy make and smell faintly of evergreen trees. While worn and invested, your footsteps sound like rustling leaves, granting you a +1 item bonus to Stealth checks in a forest or wooded area. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The small roots extending from the soles of these boots allow you to move freely and easily across wood. **Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're standing on earth, and something attempts to move you against your will;  **Effect** The roots extend from your boots to grip the ground, granting you a +4 item bonus to your Fortitude DC against effects that attempt to move you, such as Shove or Pull.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 77

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact or 10 minutes (concentrate, Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This green tea is often steeped in a pot with a dried persimmon. Traditionally, all participants in a complex discussion start their conversation with a tea ceremony involving _covenant tea_, with each member of the group enjoying the covenant of the shared beverage. Some have been known to use trickery and sleight of hand to ensure only those whose goals align with the tea preparer are served _covenant tea_, while others in the group are served non-magical (but still delicious) green tea, thus subtly tipping the balance in discussion toward those the tea server favors. This practice has resulted in some regions referring to covenant tea as “trickery tea.” Regardless of what you prefer to call the tea, when you drink it, you gain a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks and to your Perception DC for 10 minutes. 

---

This sweet and refreshing tea is made by adding a mixture of honey, lemon slices, and sliced ginger. This is considered to be the bare minimum when serving _energizing tea_, and many go above and beyond by adding additional citrus fruits or berries to the mix or refusing to serve the tea at all without accompanying it with a full platter of spiced pastries and sweets. This golden tea has energizing properties and, when consumed, grants you a +1 item bonus to Athletics and Acrobatics checks for 10 minutes.

_Spiritsight tea_ exudes a soft blue glow, creating illumination equal to that of a candle. When consumed, your eyes take on a soft glow as well, and you can see invisible creatures and objects for 10 minutes; such creatures appear to you as translucent shapes, and they're [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to you. You gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) creatures. 

---

>
[Injigo's Loving Embrace](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3147)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #198: No Breath to Cry](/Sources.aspx?ID=224) pg. 77

**Price** 675 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This net was woven by the jorogumo Injigo, who presented it as a gift to her gnome sweetheart, Mara, to keep her safe in their mountain cottage when Injigo left on hunting expeditions.

 _Injigo's Loving Embrace_ functions as a typical [net](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2738). You gain a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks made to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) with the net.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You spin the net in the direction of an incorporeal creature within 30 feet that you can see. Lines of silken force whip out to lash around the incorporeal creature, who must attempt a DC 25 Reflex save to avoid becoming [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until the end of your next turn. You can Sustain this activation for up to 1 minute, and the creature must succeed at a DC 25 check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) the net.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You wrap the net around you like a blanket as you prepare to sleep. As long as you get 8 hours of sleep or analogous rest, you dream of writing love letters to someone you adore: this could be an actual paramour, someone you're interested in, or someone unknown whose identity you don't recall after waking. When you wake, you're filled with a sense of melancholia about those unsent letters, but these feelings distract you from other, more unpleasant thoughts, granting you resistance 5 to mental damage and a +1 item bonus to saving throws against mental effects for the next 8 hours.

</column>

[Kinbur's Sandals of Bounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3148)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #198: No Breath to Cry](/Sources.aspx?ID=224) pg. 77

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These elevated wooden sandals once belonged to a haughty kitsune named Kinburi. It was well known that her swiftness and grace were unmatched, and observers described her as seeming to glide above the earth with each step. She often challenged others to wager on her speed, but as people began to grow wise, she was forced to conceal her identity or promise to forfeit her sandals if she lost.

 These sandals give you a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378). In addition, when you use the [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) action, you can move 5 feet further if jumping horizontally or 3 feet higher if jumping vertically.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (command);  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You loudly boast about your grace and agility, then take any combination of two High Jumps or Long Jumps. You do not need to Stride first, and between the two jumps, you need only to come into contact with a physical object before making the second jump; this object doesn't need to be one that can bear your weight, or even be attached to the ground—you can jump off from a floating feather or a thin branch or even off a paper wall as needed. The sandals' item bonus increases to +2 for these jumps.

</column>

**Price** 180 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This special blend of potent herbs comes in the form of a compact ball that allows it to be held in the mouth, where it remains for 1 hour. An energizing pill has a bitter taste at first, but the longer one lets it soak, the more complex and sweet its flavor grows. It heightens your reactions, granting you a +2 item bonus to initiative rolls with Perception.

 **Secondary Effect** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** You would become [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94); **Effect** Reduce the value of the condition you just gained by 1; if this reduces the value to 0, you don't gain the triggering condition.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 75

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in one hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Composite Shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=75)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted by layering bamboo with strips of sliced scales harvested from a fire-breathing dragon, this bow has a significant draw strength. This design is commonly seen in Hongal, as the shorter limbs allow for easier maneuvering on horseback. While the wielder of this _+2 striking [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=435)_ is mounted, they apply the bow's item bonus to Nature checks to Command your mount. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You draw the bow back to its maximum draw length without nocking an arrow, and as you release the string, the _dragonfire halfbow_ casts [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1530) (heightened to 5th- level; DC 29 Reflex save), targeted at a point of your choosing within the spell's range. You and your mount are immune to the effects of this fireball.

This folding handheld paper fan appears blank when first found, but if the wielder unfolds its leaves as an Interact action, they display an ink-brush painting of the wielder's choice. The fan must be closed and opened again to display a different painting. While held, the _fan of falling words_ grants you a +2 item bonus to Performance checks to act or perform comedy, orate, or sing. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You manifest the tapestry of your words, causing the image you depict on the fan to leap off its leaves. The fan casts [_hallucinatory terrain_](/Spells.aspx?ID=145) to your specifications (DC 27 Will save to disbelieve). While this only takes three actions to perform (as opposed to the spell's normal 10 minutes of casting), the effect has no range, and the 50-foot burst it creates is centered on you.

This immaculately braided red cord is made in this tradition and can hold up to 100 coins at any given time. As long as you carry a _fortune cord_, you gain a +2 item bonus to skill checks to Earn Income. If you load up to 100 coins onto a _fortune cord_ as part of your daily preparations, you can Activate the magic item in two different ways until the next time you make your daily preparations, provided all the loaded coins are of the same type. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** you have at least 50 coins loaded onto the _fortune cord_; **Effect** You transform the fortune cord into a _+2 striking [nunchaku](/Weapons.aspx?ID=414)_ for 1 minute. The type of coin loaded onto the cord determines the additional weapon property rune that manifests on this _+2 striking [nunchaku](/Weapons.aspx?ID=414)_, as follows.
  • **Copper**: _[corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834) weapon_
  • **Silver**: _[shock](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847) weapon_
  • **Gold**: _[flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838) weapon_
  • **Platinum**: _[frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) weapon_
**Activate** manipulate, Interact; **Effect** You whip the fortune cord, causing 10 coins loaded onto it to detach and fire at a creature within 100 feet that you can see. That creature takes 4d6 damage (DC 28 basic Reflex save); the damage type depends on the type of coins you've loaded. Copper coins deal acid damage, silver coins deal electricity damage, gold coins deal fire damage, and platinum coins deal cold damage.

May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts **Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 77 **Price** 1,820 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- This ash wood staff is topped by a long tassel of bleached-white horsehair. Historically carried by the most important of court officials throughout various regions and periods of Tian Xia's history, purgatory emissary's staves are also strongly associated with psychopomps serving punitive sentences. It's thought this connection is a comical nod to the bureaucratic nature of the afterlife. Psychopomps and spirits tend to regard you with a level of respect while you carry a _purgatory emissary's staff_. While you wield this staff, you receive a +2 item bonus to all skill checks made to adjust a psychopomp's or spirit's attitude. When used as a weapon, a purgatory emissary's staff is a _+2 striking [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)_. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
  • **Cantrip** [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79)
  • **1st** [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470), [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1660)
  • **2nd** [_remove fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=252), [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271)
  • **3rd** [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269), [_zone of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=379)
  • **4th** [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493), [_talking corpse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1712)

Special cells in your skin can change color to help you blend in with your environment. You gain the listed item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) and [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404).

**Activate—Background Adaptation** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For 1 minute, you can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) without needing [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to do so. This doesn’t allow you to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) without ending your movement in cover or concealment, however, as your skin’s attempts to match the background as you move produce noticeable rippling waves of color.

This _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [klar](/Shields.aspx?ID=12)_ is fashioned from the skull of a hippopotamus, with one of its canines acting as the blade. While wielding a _hippopotamus klar_, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks.

**Activate—Engulfing Jaws** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The hippo jaws of the shield open impossibly wide. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with the klar blade targeting two creatures adjacent to each other. Roll the attack and damage once and apply it to each creature separately. This counts as two attacks for your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the entire skull of a [hippopotamus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=699).

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 105 2.0 **Price** 2,600 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** 2 --- The main portion of this set of bagpipes is fashioned from the dried skin of a [cauthooj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2870), with the feathers still attached. The bird’s vocal cords are crafted into the instrument’s reeds. The pipes grant a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks while playing music with them. **Activate—Disorienting Fugue** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You play several notes on the pipes, quickly altering their pitch and tone. Each creature within a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must attempt a DC 31 Will save to resist the song. Creatures that attempt this save become temporarily immune to Disorienting Fugue for 1 minute. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and its temporary immunity to Disorienting Fugue increases to 1 hour.
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** The target is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The target is confused for 1 round and immediately attacks itself (in the normal fashion for attacking oneself while confused). This [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) doesn’t give the creature a flat check to recover from the confusion. **Activate—Throw Song** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet attempts a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against you or an ally; **Effect** You let loose a staccato chirp from the pipes that appears to come from somewhere else. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 31 Will save. On a failure, the creature redirects the Strike to another creature of your choice within reach of the melee Strike. If no other creatures are within range, the affected creature instead takes a –2 penalty to the Strike. **Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the skin and vocal cords of a [cauthooj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2870).

This glass amulet is set on a steel backing shaped like a cage and flickers with an eerie crimson glow. Magically sealed within is a portion of a hellcat's ever-burning heart. While wearing the amulet, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks made while in [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407), and you can cast the [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1585) cantrip emanating from the amulet as an [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232) divine spell.

**Activate—Invisible Pounce** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You are in bright light; **Effect** You become [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to your speed, and then make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) at the end of that movement. After making the Strike, you are no longer invisible. If at any point during your Stride, you pass out of [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402), you are no longer invisible and must stop moving. You may make a melee Strike if you have a target within reach.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the heart of a [hellcat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=695).

You sprout a second head, increasing your awareness, intuition, and cognitive ability but also causing your physical capabilities to be impaired as both minds struggle to control a single body.

**Benefit** For 10 minutes, you gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) and a +3 item bonus to all Intelligence- and Wisdom-based skill checks. Once during the mutagen's effect, if you fail or critically fail a Will saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, you can treat the result as one degree of success better.

Your eyes bulge from their sockets and extend upwards from your head on long, prehensile stalks, greatly enhancing your eyesight and field of view but leaving you unable to close your eyes, increasing your vulnerability to harmful visual effects.

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

---

Made with a brightly colored leather strap, these goggles have a series of overlapping lenses in an array of colors spanning the spectrum of visible light. The effect of this is that every color is more vibrant and similar shades have higher contrast. This means that shapes of even similar colors tend to stand out more, allowing the wearer to see even camouflage easier.

As an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action, you can set the lenses to make things stand out at your current location. Until you move, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) checks when you [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301).

This suit of _+1 [splint mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=48)_ is worn by veteran sailors aboard warships who want as much protection as possible but still need to remain mobile enough to [climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) up rigging or [swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) should the need arise. Your mind becomes clear, but physical matters seem ephemeral. 

**Benefit** You gain an item bonus to Arcana, Crafting, Lore, Occultism, and Society checks and all checks to Recall Knowledge. Your critical failures on [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) checks become failures instead. 

**Drawback** You take a –2 penalty to weapon and unarmed attack rolls, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks, and [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks. You can carry 2 less Bulk than normal before becoming [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=70), and the maximum Bulk you can carry is reduced by 4.

<traits>

<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=589" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=808" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 289

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Your mind becomes clear, but physical matters seem ephemeral. 

**Benefit** You gain an item bonus to Arcana, Crafting, Lore, Occultism, and Society checks and all checks to Recall Knowledge. Your critical failures on [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) checks become failures instead. 

**Drawback** You take a –2 penalty to weapon and unarmed attack rolls, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks, and [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks. You can carry 2 less Bulk than normal before becoming [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=70), and the maximum Bulk you can carry is reduced by 4.

**Drawback** You take damage equal to twice your level; you can't recover Hit Points lost in this way by any means while the mutagen lasts. You take a –2 penalty to Fortitude saves.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Skinstitch Salve](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3359)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 296

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This sticky salve stubbornly holds wounds closed and encourages swift natural healing. You can activate the salve in either of the following ways.

**Activate—Administer Stitch** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) without requiring healer's tools. You can either gain a +2 item bonus to the Medicine check or use the salve's Medicine modifier of +13 instead of your own.

**Activate—Stitch Wounds** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You gain a +2 item bonus to the triggering Medicine check. If you roll a success on the Medicine check, you get a critical success instead.

</column>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 308 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- A large, stylized symbol of an eye adorns the top of this wooden staff, representing the watchful eye of the divine powers. The bearer of the staff can guide and protect, seeing bounties and tragedies that could befall them in the future. When wielding this staff, you gain a +1 item bonus to Survival checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406) or [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) and to Religion checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367). **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells. Staff of Providence **Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 308, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 2.0 **Price** 230 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **Cantrip** [_guidance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1549)
  • **1st** [_bless_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1451), [_create water_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1476)
  • **2nd** [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1445), [_create food_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1475), [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663), [_status_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1690)

  • **3rd** [_safe passage_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1659), [_wanderer's guide_](/Spells.aspx?ID=368)
  • **4th** [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467), [_dispelling globe_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1494), _status_
Staff of Providence (Major) **Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 308, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 2.0 **Price** 4,100 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **5th** _dispelling globe_, [_scouting eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1661), _see the unseen_
  • **6th** _dispelling globe_, [_scintillating safeguard_](/Spells.aspx?ID=713), [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727)
Staff of Providence (True) **Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 308, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 2.0 **Price** 64,000 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **7th** _dispelling globe_, [_energy aegis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1512)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 310, [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 605 <sup>4.0</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These brass goggles are engraved with flame patterns and have thick, heavy lenses. While worn, they give you a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) alchemical items. When making [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with alchemical bombs, you ignore lesser [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) . If your Strike with an alchemical bomb fails (but doesn't critically fail), you gain a +1 item bonus to the splash damage the target of the Strike takes.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 310

**Price** 940 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black, metal ring is inset with rubies that occasionally give off wisps of smoke. It grants you a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks.

**Activate—Fire Jump** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You Stride (or Burrow or Fly, if you have the corresponding Speed) into any fire large enough to contain you, including magical fires. You vanish into the fire and take no damage from it. You can sense all sufficiently large fires within 100 feet of where you vanish, and you reemerge from any of those fires, either within the fire or adjacent to it. If you end your movement in the fire, it affects you as normal.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 310

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magic ring seems like simple tarnished brass, but it enhances your curiosity about traps and devices of all kinds. ---

This humble sash can be worn around the waist or across the chest. A sash of prowess often bears a coloration or a pattern that represents the monastery in which you trained but can also sport religious symbology, such as the open hand of Irori. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) skill checks.

**Activate—Effortless Mastery** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You succeed at an Acrobatics or Athletics skill check; **Effect** You critically succeed instead.

**Activate—Reserves of Inner Strength** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a qi spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.

**Craft Requirements** You're a monk who can cast qi spells.

This _+2 greater striking [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841) [sawtooth saber](/Weapons.aspx?ID=423)_ has a red hilt and a purple-black blade. Favored by Red Mantis assassins who enjoy using illusions to confound their targets, a crimson bluff constantly flickers and flashes, creating brief afterimages that can be quite distracting. If you use a crimson bluff as part of a gesture when you [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), you gain a +2 item bonus to your Deception check. 

**Activate—Shimmer Step** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_blur_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1455) and then you Step or Stride. 

**Activate—Swap Places** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** oncer per day; **Trigger** An enemy would hit you with a melee Strike; **Requirements** You are under the effects of _blur_; **Effect** You swiftly dodge to the side as a momentary image of yourself manifests to distract the foe. The triggering Strike uses the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of the attack roll. The duration of your _blur_ effect is reduced by 2 rounds.

</column>

---

he traditional headwear for the Red Mantis assassin is the _mask of the mantis_. Most of these masks are constructed from hard leather helmets that serve to obscure the assassin's identity and give them the appearance of possessing a mantis's head. Some variants, however, consist only of the mask itself, and are meant to be worn over the face. Regardless of the shape and style, all _masks of the mantis_ function the same.

 Members of the Vernai can use any mask of the mantis to enhance their frightening presence—something they often do simply to reveal their standing in the society without speaking a word, as detailed fully in the entry for Vernai's Ire activation below.

 While wearing a _mask of the mantis_, you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate—Enhance Vision** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast either [_darkvision_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1481) or [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) on yourself.

**Activate—Vernai's Ire** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** You are a member of the Vernai; **Effect** You cause the mask of the mantis's eyes to shimmer with crimson light, granting yourself a far more harrowing visage. This light creates illumination equivalent to that of a candle. You can use this ability again to extinguish the frightening glow, but as long as Vernai's Ire remains active, you gain a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks.

This polished golden bracelet is formed around the scale of a famous dragon. The bracelet is etched with esoteric symbols or words—always in [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2)—that indicate kinship with dragons. As many types of _dragon rune bracelets_ exist as there are types of dragons, though dragon rune bracelets associated with [Uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=159) or [Rare](/Traits.aspx?ID=137) dragons are Rare.

 While wearing a dragon rune bracelet, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks while interacting with dragons of the same type as the pendant's scale (such as [red dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=168) or [cloud dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=176)). You also gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=110) effects from any kind of [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You can cast bloodline spells from the [draconic bloodline](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=5), such as from the [sorcerer](/Classes.aspx?ID=11) class or [sorcerer multiclass archetype](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=11); **Effect** You regain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a sorcerer bloodline spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of your turn, it is lost.

An _exploration lens_ is a magical glass lens designed for a [bull's-eye lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=29). <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Grit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1494)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Drug" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=261" />
<trait label="Ingested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Absalom, City of Lost Omens](/Sources.aspx?ID=108) pg. 391

**Price** 3 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

First developed in the Puddles about 20 years ago, this stimulant has grown from a diversion of the wretched poor to a habit for well- heeled merchants and nobles. At low doses, grit provides the physical body with increased energy while stimulating the idle mind into effortless flights of creative fancy. Abuse of the drug leads to severe hallucinations, numbing, and uncontrollable rage. Grit is produced by grinding down alchemically-enhanced barbarian chew, which is mixed with toxic plant- based substances, such as bitterbark or redroot. The powder is very expensive and highly addictive.

The save for addiction to grit is DC 15, and the addiction has the [virulent](/Traits.aspx?ID=162) trait.

 **Saving Throw** DC 15 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 4 hours; **Stage 1** +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks (10 minutes); **Stage 2** +1 item bonus to Athletics, Crafting, and Performance checks, –2 item penalty to Perception checks (1 hour); **Stage 3** –4 item penalty to Perception checks (1 hour); **Stage 4** as stage 3 (1 hour); **Stage 5** [confusion](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) (1 round); **Stage 6** [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) (remaining duration)

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Grit
primary_source_raw: Absalom, City of Lost Omens pg. 391

[Demon Dust](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1495)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Drug" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=261" />
<trait label="Inhaled" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=96" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Absalom, City of Lost Omens](/Sources.aspx?ID=108) pg. 391

**Price** 45 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This highly addictive drug is produced from the crushed bones of [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28). Demon dust strengthens the inhaler's body for acts requiring great physical stamina. While the drug is in effect, users typically experience some form of memory loss. Others claim to have experienced hallucinations, flashbacks, and confusion for a few hours after the drug wears off.

The save for addiction to demon dust is DC 24, and the addiction has the [virulent](/Traits.aspx?ID=162) trait.

 **Saving Throw** DC 20 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 8 hours; **Stage 1** +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and treat up to 4 Bulk as being negligible in weight (1 minute); **Stage 2** +2 item bonus to Athletics checks, treat up to 4 Bulk as being negligible in weight, and [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) (1 hour); **Stage 3** stupefied 1 (1 hour); **Stage 4** stupefied 2 (1 hour); **Stage 5** stupefied 2 and all memories made since you were first exposed to this dose of demon dust become hazy and vague (1 hour); **Stage 6** stupefied 2 and all memories made in the previous 24 hours become hazy and vague (1 hour)

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The followers of the Broken Tusk have passed down their custom of crafting and gifting these small ivory necklaces for generations. They're typically made from mammoth tusk (though any type of ivory will do), and each is carved to resemble a particular kind of animal—usually a raven, a moose, an ox, or an otter. Because tradition dictates that Broken Tusk followers take ivory only from already-dead animals, _Broken Tusk pendants_ are especially rare; if an individual loses their pendant, it might be years before they acquire the materials necessary to fashion a replacement. _Broken Tusk pendants_ bear no magical powers if they are made for oneself; only gifted pendants have true magical properties.

 You wear a _Broken Tusk pendant_ like jewelry or tie it to your clothing. A _Broken Tusk pendant_ grants you a +1 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks; this bonus increases to +2 when you [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) of the specific kind depicted by the pendant.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) targets you with a melee attack, and you can see the animal;  **Effect** You gain a +1 item bonus to AC against the triggering attack, or a +2 item bonus if the animal is the specific kind depicted by the pendant.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Detection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=43" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 19

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This golden ring is sculpted with the visage of a grinning skull on the side. While wearing the ring, you can attempt to detect the presence of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creatures as an [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66) activity. This reveals the presence or absence of undead in the area, but it doesn't pinpoint their locations. This ring can't detect undead whose appearance is masked by any [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) spell that is 2nd level or higher. If an undead is hiding or disguised, the GM rolls a secret Perception check for you against the undead's [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) or [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC, as appropriate, with a +2 item bonus to your check.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision ([positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You gain the [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) condition from an undead creature;  **Effect** Reduce the value of the drained condition you gain by 1, and the undead that caused the condition takes 2d6 positive damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shadows at Sundown](/Sources.aspx?ID=121) pg. 53

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A horn of the sun aurochs grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks when played as an instrument.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The horn is clearly audible for hundreds of feet, but within a 20-foot emanation, the sound causes agony in those who wish harm upon the user; the horn also sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in that area and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) to the next 20 feet. Enemies of the user in this area take 7d6 sonic damage and 7d6 good damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 30 Fortitude save). Creatures that are specifically vulnerable to sunlight are also [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) if they fail this save or frightened 2 on a critical failure. This activation also attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) any [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) or [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) effects in the area (+23 counteract check).

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to medium or heavy armor

</row>

---

Parade armor is an armor adjustment that creates a set of pseudo-decorative armor to wear during noncombat functions. Any medium or heavy armor can be fashioned into parade armor, which features custom designs based on the wearer's affiliation, military branch, or rank. A particular faction typically has one uniform appearance for its set of parade armor. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against creatures of the same affiliation as your parade armor, though the bonus to Intimidation doesn't apply when interacting with creatures of higher rank than you. The armor is slightly bulkier, increasing the Bulk by 1.

[Busine of Divine Reinforcement](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1566)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Good" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=83" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 89

**Price** 6,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long, straight, trumpet-like instrument is made of well-polished brass and adorned with imagery of angels fighting demons or religious symbols. When played as an instrument, the busine generates powerful and harmonious notes and grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You play a few notes on the busine. Evil creatures within 60 feet who hear the notes must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or be [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) for 1 round, or 2 rounds on a critical failure; this is an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You blow into the busine and conjure a [celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16) with the effects of a 6th-level [_summon celestial_](/Spells.aspx?ID=317) spell, but there are no alignment restrictions to define which celestials you can call. The celestial will fight only evil creatures and leaves after all present evil creatures have been defeated or the spell's duration ends, whichever comes first. You can Sustain the Activation to extend the spell's duration, as normal. If you have a deity and the conjured celestial's alignment is one of your deity's preferred alignments, the effect functions as a normal 6th-level _summon celestial_ spell instead, meaning the celestial will fight any creature, not just evil creatures, and will perform other tasks as you command.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 574 <sup>4.0</sup>

**Price** 22,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An array of semiprecious stones is set into the ornate silver and beaten copper cover of this thick and weighty tome. If you open the book before it’s been activated, its vellum pages are blank and pristine, but once activated, words dance and swim onto the pages before your eyes.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);     **Effect** As you flip through the book, you think about a broad topic you want to know more about. Choose one skill: Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or a single subcategory of Lore. The book’s pages fill with information about that skill, though only you can see the information. While the pages are full, you can spend an Interact action perusing the book just before attempting a check to Recall Knowledge with the chosen skill. This grants you a +3 item bonus to the check, and if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. The information within the book disappears after 24 hours or when the tome is activated again.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This sturdy leather saddle was designed to improve communication between mount and rider, allowing even inexperienced knights to command their mounts in battle. A swiftmount saddle grants a +2 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks made to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) for anyone who is riding the creature wearing it.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You're adjacent to the creature wearing the _swiftmount saddle_ and could [Mount](/Actions.aspx?ID=96) it; **Effect** You Mount the creature wearing the _swiftmount saddle_.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hoax-Hunter's Kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1616)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 63

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wooden box unfolds into a stack of hinged trays holding calipers, magnifying lenses, acids and reagents, comparison sketches of species commonly mistaken for one another, and glass slides for specimen testing. When you use this kit to study accounts of a creature or what it left behind (such as spoor, tracks, or fur samples), you gain a +1 item bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about the creature or to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the creature. In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the creature (but don't critically fail), you're able to eliminate at least one possibility of a common type of animal. For instance, you might be able to verify the creature isn't an [owlbear](/Monsters.aspx?ID=328), even if you get no further information.

</column>

text: <title level="1" right="Item 3" pfs="Standard" > Hoax-Hunter's Kit Source Dark Archive pg. 63 Price 50 gp Hands 2 Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 1 --- This wooden box unfolds into a stack of hinged trays holding calipers, magnifying lenses, acids and reagents, comparison sketches of species commonly mistaken for one another, and glass slides for specimen testing. When you use this kit to study accounts of a creature or what it left behind (such as spoor, tracks, or fur samples), you gain a +1 item bonus to Recall Knowledge about the creature or to Track the creature. In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the creature (but don't critically fail), you're able to eliminate at least one possibility of a common type of animal. For instance, you might be able to verify the creature isn't an owlbear, even if you get no further information.

<traits>

<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn ring

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

Smiling faces are inscribed about this silver band. You become a fluent weaver of fictions, gaining a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks for storytelling. Whenever you're under suspicion or being questioned by an authority figure, you find yourself compulsively spinning absurd, tall tales that are so unconvincing that they make you look guilty even when you're innocent. The ring's bonuses vanish, and any listener can quickly determine you're lying. Nevertheless, you're completely unable to be honest in such situations.

>
[Self-Emptying Pocket](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1656)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 165

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You never perform to an empty crowd after promising any profits to a phantom in a playhouse, sealed by holes that appear in your pockets. By meeting with the attendees at your events, you can use [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49). When you would use Performance to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23), you don't earn any gold pieces, as the money disappears before you can even count it.

 The entity that holds your _bargained contract_ can influence your reception any time you perform for a crowd or Activate the pocket. If they influence your performance favorably, you gain a +2 item bonus to your Performance check. If they influence your performance unfavorably, you gain a -2 item penalty to your Performance check. If you've failed to earn the entity money in quite a while, it typically influences your performance unfavorably.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You exercise all of your charm on a creature, turning a chance meeting into an impromptu performance that commands attention. Attempt a single Performance check against the Perception DC of the creature. On a success, the creature is affected as though by a successful Deception check to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=45). The entity that holds your contract can influence this performance as well.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A nigh-infinite assortment of games exist in Golarion. Simple games, including dice, a deck of cards, or dominoes, cost 5 sp. Board games vary in cost from 1 gp for dexterity games like Bungle, 3 gp for colorful children's games like Cauldron Quest, and 5 gp for complex strategy games like Kingmaker and Abendego Raiders. Lavish game sets can cost much more than these prices, as they are made of expensive components and are intricately crafted works of art unto themselves.

These dice are weighted on one side to ensure they always land with the desired number facing up. Loaded dice grant you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks to gamble with the dice. You can determine a die is loaded while handling it with a successful secret DC 20 Perception check. Determining dice are loaded without handling the dice is more difficult, especially since smart cheaters switch loaded dice in and out so they don't suspiciously roll the same number over and over. In this case, an observer must succeed at a secret Perception check against the roller's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC to notice the switches or the patterns.

A _maestro's chair_ is a [traveler's chair](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1356) with the [impulse control](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1361) upgrade and a small pipe organ installed into the frame. You can use the maestro's chair to make [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks in the same manner that you could use any mundane instrument, using both of your hands. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 92

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn under light armor or clothes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Adventurers have found a number of uses for these animal blood–filled bladders, which were originally used in theatrical productions. Whenever you take slashing or piercing damage with the fake blood pack under your clothes or armor, roll a DC 11 flat check. On a success, the blood pack is punctured. You or an ally can puncture the hidden pack intentionally. When faking an injury, the blood pack grants a +2 item bonus to relevant [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks, such as to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) about being injured. Abilities that trigger when a creature deals bleed damage, determine if a creature is bleeding, or are otherwise based on bleed damage don't trigger or apply for blood from a fake blood pack, which might mean creatures with such abilities automatically realize the ruse.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs=""
>
[Oculus of Abaddon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1747)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 587

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _oculus of Abaddon_ is a potent artifact rumored to have been created by one of the [Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=11) as a way to reward those who work as their agents on the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). More likely, these items were crafted by a powerful pre-Earthfall death cult that has long since moved on, leaving behind these dangerous artifacts to tempt mortals into serving the needs of the Horsemen. 

An _oculus of Abaddon_ appears as a sphere of clear crystal that contains a pinpoint of flickering red light at its center. When held, the oculus feels warm to the touch and fills you with a sudden desire to pluck out an eye and place the oculus within the socket—this causes 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Once placed in an eye socket, the oculus can be removed only by ripping it free (causing the same amount of persistent bleed damage as the initial plucking). When you place the oculus in your empty eye socket, you immediately heal all damage caused by plucking the previous eye out. Once placed, an oculus grants you constant [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415). It can also be activated to perform a number of other magical effects, as detailed below, but if you aren't evil, each time you activate an _oculus of Abaddon_, you must succeed at a DC 36 Will save or become affected by a [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=314) (heightened to 8th level) to perform an evil act the next time an opportunity to do so arises, as determined by the GM.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision);  **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You gain the effects of [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), heightened to 7th level.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You use the _oculus of Abaddon_ to cast a [_planar binding_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=17) ritual, heightened to 7th level. You can only conjure neutral evil creatures with this casting of _planar binding_. If you already know the _planar binding_ ritual, you gain a +3 item bonus on the primary check when casting _planar binding_.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision;    **Requirements** you have a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) or [animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=149); **Effect** You can see and hear through your familiar or animal companion's eyes and ears, provided you are on the same plane. This effect can be sustained, but as long as you do so you can take no other actions.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (envision; [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64)) **Frequency** once per year;   **Effect** You manipulate the minds of a huge number of targets, provided that the end goal of the manipulation is a tragic or otherwise horrific fate for those being manipulated. This functions as [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315), but with a range of 1 mile. All creatures within this area are affected, with the same suggestion implanted in their minds. Creatures hear the telepathic suggestion in their native language, and creatures that are 7th level or higher can attempt a DC 36 Will save to resist the effect. This power was used by Vordakai to cause the vanishing of Varnhold, suggesting to its inhabitants to leave their homes and travel south to his tomb. If this effect is [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) or removed on one victim, it ends for all victims.

**Destruction** A foul and hideous object, an _oculus of Abaddon_ is fortunately relatively easy to destroy, as far as artifacts go. It has Hardness 25 and 100 Hit Points, but repairs damage to itself swiftly, regaining 10 Hit Points per round. It has weakness 10 to bludgeoning damage and weakness 30 to good damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Oculus of Abaddon

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 589

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ring, carved from green wood, bears carvings of tigers chasing each other through grasslands and forests. _Rings of the tiger_ are traditionally crafted by Kellids in northeastern Avistan, and are often worn by scouts or explorers. Many barbarians in these regions react poorly to anyone obviously not part of their people who dare to wear such a ring, but ironically have been known to gift these rings to outsiders who have proven their worth—potentially setting up a further clash in the future should that character encounter another group of Kellids who aren't familiar with how the wearer earned the right to wear the ring. A ring of the tiger grants a +1 item bonus on [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks and Perception checks made in outdoor wilderness areas, and it can be activated to momentarily transform the wearer's hand into a tiger's claw.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;    **Requirements** You aren't carrying anything in the hand on which the ring is worn; **Effect** Your hand becomes a tiger's claw, granting you an [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) claw [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that inflicts 1d6 slashing damage, and you Strike with the claw. Then the claw turns back to normal.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 589

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This impressive-looking helmet is crafted to resemble the skull of a mighty stag. Although made from bone, the antlers and helm are as strong as iron. While the Stag Lord himself wears this helmet in the Kingmaker Adventure Path, _stag's helms_ are actually the creation of the church of [Erastil](/Deities.aspx?ID=6), and worshipers of this deity find that the helm is not only particularly comfortable to wear, but that they can activate it once per hour rather than once per day.

 Rather than restrict the senses, a _stag's helm_ enhances them, causing the world to appear in more vibrant colors and significantly enhancing the ambient sounds of the region without making them distracting. While worn, it grants a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" />  ;  **Frequency** once per day (or once per hour if the wearer worships Erastil);   **Effect** Choose a single creature within 30 feet. The _stag's helm_ focuses your aim and grants supernatural insight into your next shot. Your target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to the next ranged Strike you make this turn against them.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

The blade of this _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=20)_ shimmers with a prismatic sheen, as if faintly reflecting a rainbow. A _songbird's brush_ sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 40 feet). When wielded in combat, the sound of the blade cutting through the air creates a soft, musical trill as if produced by a songbird. Sacred to the faithful of [Shelyn](/Deities.aspx?ID=17), a _songbird's brush_ is so named for the fighting style developed by worshippers of the Eternal Rose, which equates its sweeping swings to painting with a brush. A songbird's brush grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks made to dance or sing as long as the glaive is held in two hands.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You sweep the _songbird's brush_ in an arc before you, casting [_prismatic spray_](/Spells.aspx?ID=233) from the glaive. The spell DC is 34. This _prismatic spray_ does not affect good-aligned creatures in its area.

**Craft Requirements** You are a worshipper of Shelyn.

May contain spoilers from Blood Lords **Source** [Pathfinder #185: A Taste of Ashes](/Sources.aspx?ID=188) pg. 78 **Price** 1,600 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands or mounted **Bulk** 3 --- This drum-shaped metal floodlight has a metal handle on each side and a housing at its base to be slotted into a stand or pedestal. A _splendid floodlight_ has a primary function as well as several secondary functions available by rotating through a series of translucent sheets called gels. [Shadewither Key](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1818)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Shadow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=143" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #187: The Seventh Arch](/Sources.aspx?ID=192) pg. 79

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This palm-sized talisman hangs on a string of braided bark fibers. It resembles a leaf from some unknown tree similar to oak, carved from jade and then dipped halfway into black ink that looks wet despite feeling completely dry. The gate key was originally created to open the aiudara known as the _Seventh Arch_. In recent years, corrupting magic has given it additional, stranger powers.

 When you wear and invest _the Shadewither Key_, shadows gather around you. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks. However, this boon comes with great risk: any [elf](/Traits.aspx?ID=58) who touches _the Shadewither Key_ is immediately afflicted with the [_obnubilate curse_](/Curses.aspx?ID=49).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You touch _the Shadewither Key_ and command the shadows it casts around you to peel away. The shadows form an umbral double that resembles you in every way except for its fiery red eyes and the expression of wicked delight on its face. The double occupies the same space as you and attempts to intercept any attacks aimed at you. A creature must succeed at a DC 11 flat check when targeting you with an attack, spell, or other effect; on a failure, they hit the shadowy double instead of you. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the double is hit, whichever comes first. Once the double is hit, it's destroyed. As long as the double exists, you don't gain _the Shadewither Key's_ item bonus to Stealth checks.

**Destruction** _The Shadewither Key's_ magic can be destroyed by exposing the artifact to uncontained teleportation energies. If touched to an unlinked or malfunctioning _aiudara_, _the Shadewither Key_ causes the gate to connect to a new counterpart. If this happens, the key's magic leaves it, rendering the item useless.

</column>

>
[Bastion of the Inheritor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1841)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 14 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 1,750 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 5
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Bastion Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=17)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Worn by [Iomedae's](/Deities.aspx?ID=9) prestigious knights, this _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [bastion plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=17)_ is emblazoned with the Inheritor's [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) and sports a white cloak. While the cloak is white, this armor grants you a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50), provided your target has no enmity toward Iomedae.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** The armor's cloak becomes red for 1 minute. As long as the cloak is red, you gain the benefits of the armor's deflect melee trait without needing to spend an additional action to activate it during each turn.

**Craft Requirements** You worship Iomedae.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 19 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 230 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Hide Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=7)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This suit of _+1 [hide armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=7)_ is sickly green and covered in thick warts and nodules, fashioned from the hide of a [trollhound](/Monsters.aspx?ID=835) and imbued with some of the beast's vitality. Wearing this armor gives you a –1 circumstance penalty to all checks made using [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to interact with [trolls](/Monsters.aspx?ID=395) and a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks used to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) in communities traditionally plagued by troll attacks.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;   **Trigger** You take damage from a melee attack while you have half or fewer of your normal maximum Hit Points;  **Effect** Your body knits itself back together, healing you for 3d8 Hit Points.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hides of at least two trollhounds.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
