Each _specialist's ring_ is dedicated to a single school of magic, and the ring is covered in symbols and glyphs related to that school according to the creator's arcane studies. A _specialist's ring_ has the trait corresponding to its school of magic. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) checks, and a +1 circumstance bonus to recognize magical effects and items of the specific school of magic.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a wizard school spell of the corresponding school. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

[Stampede Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1080)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 190 <sup>1.1</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon's heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon Concentrates on the medallion and their connection to you, allowing them to momentarily manifest into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an emanation around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon's Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

>
[Thousand-Blade Thesis](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1081)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 191 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This collection of lacquered rice paper scrolls mounted on flexible bamboo contains a wealth of calligraphic essays and paintings on the art of war, specifically focused on the use of various weapons in warfare and how to tactically deploy warriors using those weapons to the best possible advantage. Consulting the thesis grants a +2 item bonus to [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks. Like most scholarly compendiums, this usage requires holding the thesis in one hand.

 The thesis also serves as an extradimensional armory for weapons and ammunition. The thesis has a capacity of 5 Bulk, and only weapons and ammunition can be stored within it. You and others can Interact with the thesis to store or retrieve a weapon or piece of ammunition in it, like a mundane container.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _thousand-blade thesis_ dramatically unfurls, and the weapons contained within it spring forth and array themselves impressively in the air, floating within easy reach. For 1 minute, you can use a free action to Interact to draw one of the floating weapons. Others can attempt to nab them out of the air, but to do so they must critically succeed at a [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) check. You can't place weapons back into the thesis until the minute elapses.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 75, [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 151 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn crown

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Stories tell of a forgotten king who once loved his subjects so much he was willing to give his own life energy for them. Whether true or not, this majestic wooden crown bears elaborate carvings depicting that tale. It's ringed with images of the same kingly figure giving more and more of himself to a throng of needy subjects. While wearing it, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You bow to an ally within 30 feet, creating a magical bond between the two of you. You cast [_shield other_](/Spells.aspx?ID=281) targeting the ally. The link remains even if you move more than 30 feet away from them. At the end of the spell's duration, your ally recovers 4d8 Hit Points and you recover half of what they recover.

</column>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Night of the Gray Death</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 53

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5+"
    pfs=""
>
[Spirit-Singer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1138)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 83 <sup>2.0</sup>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Etheric spirit-singers create an eerie spectral sound based on the presence of spiritual essence and other ethereal energies. All spirit-singers can be used as musical instruments by manipulating the sensitivity to ethereal energies. However, they have an even greater benefit in areas heavy with spiritual essence. When played in the presence of a significant spiritual disturbance, such as a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), a spirit-singer grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. While playing a spirit-singer, you also gain a +1 item bonus to checks to detect a haunt or incorporeal undead, and you can roll a check to notice a haunt even if you aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) for it, due to the distortions of the spirit-singer's music. A haunt or incorporeal undead that is intelligent enough to notice the effects it is having on the spirit-singer's music and that can't otherwise communicate with the living might choose to use the spirit-singer to do so if it wishes. For instance, it could try to guide the spirit-singer player towards a location by creating distortions in that direction or, if it understands language, it could try to answer questions by creating one distortion for yes and two distortions for no. Unless stated otherwise in its usage entry, a spirit-singer functions like a heavy [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37); rather than carrying it, the musician places the spirit-singer in a particular position and uses both hands to play.

When played in the presence of a significant spiritual disturbance, such as a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), a spirit-singer grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. While playing a spirit-singer, you also gain a +1 item bonus to checks to detect a haunt or incorporeal undead, and you can roll a check to notice a haunt even if you aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) for it, due to the distortions of the spirit-singer's music. A haunt or incorporeal undead that is intelligent enough to notice the effects it is having on the spirit-singer's music and that can't otherwise communicate with the living might choose to use the spirit-singer to do so if it wishes. For instance, it could try to guide the spirit-singer player towards a location by creating distortions in that direction or, if it understands language, it could try to answer questions by creating one distortion for yes and two distortions for no. Unless stated otherwise in its usage entry, a spirit-singer functions like a heavy [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37); rather than carrying it, the musician places the spirit-singer in a particular position and uses both hands to play.

[Violet Ray](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1139)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 83 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Price** 1,893 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

One of the many wondrous devices brought into the world by Stasian technology is the seemingly miraculous violet ray. Physicians claim it anything from headaches to heartburn, or nausea to deafness, all with an easy and painless treatment. The device is a glass vacuum with an insulated handle connected to a small Stasian coil. When powered, the glass tube fills with purple light and becomes warm to the touch. Pressing the tube to one's body is said to increase blood flow, eliminate toxins, and many other beneficial effects. A violet ray functions as a set of [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) and provides a +2 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) checks to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54), [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=55), [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=56), or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57).

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You apply the violet ray to an adjacent creature and attempt to counteract the [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) condition with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) level of 6 and a counteract modifier of +22, using the source of the condition to determine the condition's counteract level and DC. If the condition was caused by an ongoing effect and you don't remove that effect, the condition returns after 1 minute. Each use of this ability can only counteract a single condition.

</column>

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

---

The components of this ammunition emit a strong smell when combined during its activation. A creature hit by an activated aromatic ammunition gains a distinct odor for up to 1 hour or until the scent is washed off (requiring at least a gallon of water and 10 minutes of scrubbing). Any creatures within 30 feet smell the target, allowing even those with a weak sense of smell to detect its presence, and all creatures gain a +1 item bonus to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the affected creature for as long as it has the odor. A creature that has imprecise or precise [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) doubles the range at which they can detect the target using their scent compared to the normal range of their scent.

Diving suits are bulky, waterproofed leather outfits with copper helmets, worn by divers and underwater salvagers. The suit grants a +1 item bonus to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) checks made underwater, and the helmet features tubes for connecting [_bottled air_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=250). When connected to a diving suit, bottled air doesn't need to be held and can be used to breathe as a free action. If you wear armor over a diving suit, you become [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) until you remove the diving suit.

This heavy drum is engraved along the sides with images of centaurs in fierce combat. The drum grants you a +3 item bonus on [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks you make using the drum. **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The drum casts a DC 43 [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [centaur](/Monsters.aspx?ID=76).

markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Silhouette Cloak](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1306)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 43

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

In bright light, this dark cloak shimmers with patches of color that shift and move even when the cloth is still. In dim light or darkness, the cloak seems to blend into your surroundings and grants you a +3 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Interact (1 minute);     **Effect** You and objects you wear or carry fall into your shadow, becoming a two-dimensional silhouette. In this form you aren't incorporeal, but you also don't have a solid form and don't occupy your space, allowing other creatures to pass through or end their turn there. You gain resistance 20 to all damage except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) damage, damage from effects with the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) trait, and damage from Strikes with the [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune. This increases to resistance 40 against nonmagical damage. Other creatures can't attempt Strength-based skill checks against you. Your land and climb Speeds both become 40 feet. You can't use actions except [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), Step, or Stride actions using the granted Speeds or an Interact activation to return to your normal form. If your current space doesn't have sufficient room for you to return to your normal form, you return to your normal form in the nearest open space.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You take damage;  **Effect** You fold the cloak over yourself and vanish into your shadow for a moment, gaining the benefits of the first activation until the end of the current creature's turn. The damage resistance applies to the triggering damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

While some unscrupulous chefs claim that this savory pudding is made with real dragon's blood, its crimson color and acrid smell actually come from bloody mandrake paste, ginger root, and distilled terrap sap. This potent combination singes the nostrils and throat, removing effects that make you sluggish. When you consume the pudding, it attempts a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with the listed counteract modifier to remove the [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) condition from a single source, using the source of that condition to determine the counteract level and DC.

>
[Dragon's Blood Pudding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1310)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 46

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While some unscrupulous chefs claim that this savory pudding is made with real dragon's blood, its crimson color and acrid smell actually come from bloody mandrake paste, ginger root, and distilled terrap sap. This potent combination singes the nostrils and throat, removing effects that make you sluggish. When you consume the pudding, it attempts a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with the listed counteract modifier to remove the [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) condition from a single source, using the source of that condition to determine the counteract level and DC.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The pudding has a +9 counteract modifier. You also become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32) for 1 round. While taking the additional action from being quickened, you scream, as a result of both the flavor and the mandrake paste's properties. You can use the additional action to Step, Stride, Strike, or [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53). If you choose to Demoralize, you gain a +2 item bonus to the [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check.

This sleight-of-hand for the taste buds is flavored with absinthe and honey and always resembles something completely unlike a cake, from a pile of armor to a bowl of soup. [Server's Stew](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1314)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 47

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The type of animal tongue used in this tomato-based stew shifts from region to region, but it's always cooked with spirit of wine and seasoned with [refined pesh](/Equipment.aspx?ID=626). Eating this restaurant-staff favorite empowers you to speak and understand a single language for 1 hour. This must be a language the stew's cook could speak and understand, chosen at the time of the stew's creation. It also helps your words land smoothly, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks made in that language for the same duration. It doesn't allow you to read the newly acquired language in its written form.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Server's Stew

Pickpocket's tailoring modifies an existing outfit by adding concealed interior pockets and strategically opened seams for hiding small objects inside the lining. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) of light Bulk or less in the pockets. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 50

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _quick wig_ magically conceals your natural hair while worn, eliminating the need to braid or pin your hair beneath it. In addition, your facial hair and eyebrows change color to match the wig while you wear it. When used as part of a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) to go unrecognized by changing your hair, you no longer require a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19), you gain a +1 item bonus on the check, and you reduce the time to create the disguise from 10 minutes to 5 minutes. You still need a disguise kit and the full time if you're using cosmetics and other props to change other aspects of your disguise or Impersonating a specific person, and the wig only provides its item bonus when Impersonating a specific person if that person's hair color and style match the wig's. _Quick wigs_ detangle themselves while not in use.

---

This large stone eye is the size of a fist and decorated with elaborate carvings of robes and other garments.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> (1 minute) envision, Interact;     **Effect** You enter a brief trance in which you envision yourself entering a large dressing room. You maneuver through the endless dressing-room mindscape and search for whatever articles of clothing, accessories, and other garments you desire. After the activation, you gain the effects of [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), except that it only causes you to appear to be wearing the exact outfit you selected within the mindscape. The illusion also disguises the _wardrobe stone_ to match your outfit and not appear out of place, such as by appearing to be a glove or bracelet, though it continues to occupy your hand while you're under the effects of _illusory disguise_. You can actively Dismiss the Spell, but the effects are also dismissed immediately when you're no longer holding the _wardrobe stone_.

[Camouflage Suit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1201)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 178 <sup>2.0</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This lightweight mesh fits easily over light armor. The suit is designed to incorporate local flora and ground clutter into the mesh to help you blend in seamlessly with the environment. Due to the abrasive nature of the materials used, this item is unsuitable for use by unarmored characters. You can prepare the suit for use within your current environment by using an exploration activity that takes at least 10 minutes, but sometimes longer if the materials are hard to find or the environment is unusual enough to warrant additional difficulty in preparing camouflage that can blend with it consistently.

 A suit prepared in this manner grants you a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks while you attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) in the specific environment it has been prepared for. The suit remains usable in this manner until you rest for the night, though it doesn't grant the benefit whenever you aren't in the appropriate environment. The GM might rule that some environments are unusual enough that you can't create a camouflage suit appropriate for the environment.

text: <title level="1" right="Item 3+" pfs="" > Camouflage Suit Source Guns & Gears pg. 178 2.0 Bulk L --- This lightweight mesh fits easily over light armor. The suit is designed to incorporate local flora and ground clutter into the mesh to help you blend in seamlessly with the environment. Due to the abrasive nature of the materials used, this item is unsuitable for use by unarmored characters. You can prepare the suit for use within your current environment by using an exploration activity that takes at least 10 minutes, but sometimes longer if the materials are hard to find or the environment is unusual enough to warrant additional difficulty in preparing camouflage that can blend with it consistently. A suit prepared in this manner grants you a +1 item bonus to Stealth checks while you attempt to Hide or Sneak in the specific environment it has been prepared for. The suit remains usable in this manner until you rest for the night, though it doesn't grant the benefit whenever you aren't in the appropriate environment. The GM might rule that some environments are unusual enough that you can't create a camouflage suit appropriate for the environment. <title level="2" right="Item 3" pfs="Standard" > Camouflage Suit Source Guns & Gears pg. 178 2.0 Price 10 gp Bulk L <title level="2" right="Item 9" pfs="Standard" > Camouflage Suit (Superb) Source Guns & Gears pg. 178 2.0 Price 140 gp Bulk L --- A superb camouflage suit is fashioned from especially well-blended materials and gives you a +2 item bonus to the check instead of a +1 item bonus.

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 180 <sup>2.0</sup>

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm or crossbow (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These scopes, popular with snipers and other sneaky sharpshooters who ply their trade in the dead of night, incorporate clouded crystals with magical properties into their design. While relatively useless under normal lighting conditions, these crystals can help bring things into focus when used in dim light. The scope is then given an enchantment to enhance these properties for use in darkness. The scope grants you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks involving sight in areas of dim light visible through the scope (as well as in areas of darkness, if the scope has been activated).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) until the beginning of your next turn, as long as you continue to look through the scope.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 181 <sup>2.0</sup>

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

More of a field projector than a scope, this small cylinder of magnetite has been enchanted to spread and accelerate the shrapnel of a [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=413) weapon further than the weapon's natural capabilities. Furthermore, some of the floating magnetite inside the scope's structure can help you when attempting to determine the your allies' locations. The magnetite scope grants you a +2 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) when using the scope to assist you in navigating. This scope can only be attached to firearms with the scatter trait.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** The next Strike you make this round with the gun to which the scope is attached has its scatter radius increased by 5 feet.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 182 <sup>2.0</sup>

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons. Replace the word "transmutation" in the scope of truth with the word "polymorph."_

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm or crossbow (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _scope of truth_ is a bit bigger than most to accommodate larger lenses, which have been magically prepared with tiny shards from crystal balls to reveal the truth. The scope grants you a +2 item bonus to Perception checks made to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) in areas you can see through the scope.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For the next 10 minutes, you can see things through the scope as they actually are. The GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with a +20 counteract modifier and a counteract level of 7 against any [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) or [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157) in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it, not to end the spell or effect. For instance, if the check succeeds against a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the spell.

</column>

    level="1"

>
[Crown of the Kobold King](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1727)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 114

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Originally, this magical crown was to be known as the _Crown of Toil_—a magic item crafted by the dwarven priest named Gristogar. He intended for the crown to bolster his ability to rule and herald in a new era of a dwarven kingdom that followed the teachings of [Droskar](/Deities.aspx?ID=28). Yet Gristogar wasn't equal to his own ambitions, and before he could complete the _Crown of Toil_, his cult died out and he ended his own life. For centuries, the incomplete crown lay dormant, but over that time, fragments of Gristogar's soul infused it—not enough to transform it into a truly intelligent item, but enough to give it a rudimentary need and desire to be completed.

 When the Kobold King Merlokrep discovered the discarded crown and placed it upon his head, the crown at last had agency— if not in a hale and hearty dwarf, at least in the frame of a powerful and ambitious kobold. Just as the crown began influencing Merlokrep, so too did the Kobold King's personality influence the crown. Today, the device is known as the _Crown of the Kobold King_, and while it still urges the one who wears it to build a kingdom of endlessly toiling workers, it no longer does so in honor of Droskar. Instead, it seeks the rise of a brutal kobold kingdom.

 The crown appears as a golden band surrounded by iron spikes that glisten with fresh blood—the addition of a kobold skull to the top is largely decorative, but one the crown has grown to “enjoy.” Even in its incomplete state, a few rituals away from its true potential, the _Crown of the Kobold King_ is a potent item. Wearing the crown grants you a +2 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks and a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The crown infuses you with the glorious conviction that you're meant to rule, granting you a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and Charisma-based skill checks for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast a [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208) spell.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [gauntlet](/Weapons.aspx?ID=4)_ appears little more than a dull, soot-stained, metal-plated glove at first glance, but in truth it is an invasive boon granted by [Droskar](/Deities.aspx?ID=28) to his most faithful subjects. Placing the glove on your hand causes excruciating pain as your appendage curls into a tight fist and then slowly transforms to a supernaturally hard ball of black stone, fusing to you and preventing you from using this hand for anything other than gauntlet Strikes or the _grasp of Droskar's_ activated abilities (a _grasp of Droskar_ does not have the [free-hand](/Traits.aspx?ID=181) weapon trait). The gauntlet can't be removed without a successful casting of [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) or a similar spell. The gauntlet reverts to normal (and can be removed with ease) if the curse is removed, the hand is removed from the body, or the wearer dies.

The gauntlet can't be removed without a successful casting of remove curse or a similar spell. The gauntlet reverts to normal (and can be removed with ease) if the curse is removed, the hand is removed from the body, or the wearer dies. </title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 115

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wicked-looking curved weapon is a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)_ that draws power from defeating foes, either to bolster itself or its wielder. A _heartripper blade_ is well suited for use in any ritual that involves divination, and incorporating it into any ritual with the [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) trait grants the wielder a +1 item bonus on any check made to resolve the effects of the ritual's casting.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You reduce a foe to 0 Hit Points with a Strike from the _heartripper blade_;  **Effect** The _heartripper blade_ draws power from the devastating strike, causing its blade to erupt in black flames. For 1 minute, Strikes with the _heartripper blade_ inflict an additional 1d6 negative damage to living creatures.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You reduce a foe to 0 Hit Points with a Strike from the _heartripper blade_;  **Effect** The _heartripper blade_ draws life from the victim's body and siphons it into you. Choose one of the following effects: restore 2d8 Hit Points; reduce the value of your [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) conditions by 1; or reduce the stage of one toxin or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) you're suffering by one stage (this can't reduce the stage below stage 1 or cure the affliction).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Fulu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=378" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 77 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You take the [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) action.

 
</row>

</column>

---

Tradition says the _dragonfly fulu_ should be affixed to the upper back, like the wings of an insect. When you Activate this fulu, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 minute. During this time, you can attempt an Athletics check to High Jump or Long Jump as a single action without the Stride requirement. You can also High Jump or Long Jump from a nonsolid substance, such as air or water, but if you use this power of the fulu, its effects ends after you jump.

</column>

[Elysian Dew](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2082)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 89 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 375 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you drink sweet, sky-blue _Elysian dew_, for 1 minute, you gain a 10-foot aura that evokes the vitality of [Elysium](/Planes.aspx?ID=16), causing nearby objects to seem more colorful and plants to stand taller. You and any ally that starts its turn in the emanation gain 5 temporary Hit Points, a +1 item bonus to saving throws, and a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks until the start of your or the ally's next turn. If you're evil and drink this potion, it fails to work, and you must succeed at a DC 30 Fortitude save or the potion renders you [drained 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Elysian Dew

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=116" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 61 <sup>1.1</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Developed and widely used by students at the Kitharodian Academy in Oppara, the theatrical mutagen stimulates the creative centers of your brain. This causes your movements to become exaggerated and your voice to become clear. However, the erratic surges of inspiration overload your senses, making it difficult to focus on mundane tasks.

 **Benefit** You gain the listed item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks, and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. If you're untrained in any of these skills, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level instead of +0. You also gain the listed status bonus to your Speed.

 **Drawback** You take a –1 penalty to Perception checks and Will saves. After any round where you don't spend at least 1 action to Interact with an object, [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59), Step, or Stride, you're [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the start of your next turn.

Developed and widely used by students at the Kitharodian Academy in Oppara, the theatrical mutagen stimulates the creative centers of your brain. </title>

<traits>

<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />

<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=68" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 63 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The faceplate of a dread helm has a fierce visage that magnifies the effects of fear. Cleverly concealed within is a reservoir that can hold a single [dread ampoule](/Equipment.aspx?ID=686), which takes 3 Interact actions to install. A loaded dread helm can be activated to atomize the dread ampoule, creating a fear-inducing mist that hangs around your face. The mist grants an item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks equal to the dread ampoule's item bonus. The mist also deals mental damage equal to the dread ampoule's splash damage to all creatures within a 5-foot emanation other than you. The effects last for 3 rounds, consuming the dread ampoule, and once the atomization process has begun it can't be deactivated.

</column>

This [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4) has been treated with extract from oozes, which can be reactivated in the presence of a strong acid. A receptacle in the armor can hold an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=74), which takes 3 Interact actions to install. A loaded suit of ooze skin can be activated to cause the leather to weep slippery protoplasm, granting an item bonus to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) and [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=31) checks equal to the acid flask's item bonus. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 28"
    pfs=""
>
[Philosopher's Extractor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=617)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 112

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 8
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bizarre machine is a complex arrangement of flasks, tubes, and other alchemical equipment. The _philosopher’s extractor_ is designed to create the ultimate alchemical concoctions. The extractor functions as an exceptional set of [alchemist’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2), granting a +4 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks related to alchemy. When using the extractor to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an alchemical item or with infused reagents as part of your daily preparations, you can create impeccable alchemical items. An impeccable alchemical item always uses the maximum numerical value possible for any rolls it requires, such as dealing maximum damage with [alchemist’s fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75) or restoring the maximum number of Hit Points with an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91). If the impeccable item has a duration, it lasts twice as long as normal. Finally, an impeccable alchemical item never has a drawback.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You use the extractor to produce an alchemical item of your level or lower whose formula you know. The extractor can create 56 levels’ worth of items per day in this way. For example, the extractor could create two true elixirs of life (19th level) and two moderate elixirs of life (9th level), or eight [comprehension elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88) (7th level), and so on.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (Interact);     **Effect** You take a sizable portion of a creature (at least two-thirds of its original mass) and filter it through the mechanisms of the extractor. After the end of the process, the _philosopher’s extractor_ creates a transmogrifying [mutagen](/Traits.aspx?ID=116) that imparts the essence of the creature to the drinker. The extractor can make several transmogrifying mutagens simultaneously using the same activation if enough mass is provided at once, up to a maximum of 10 concurrent mutagens. Drinking a transmogrifying mutagen imparts you with one of the creature’s unique abilities for 1 hour. This could grant one of several abilities such as a dragon’s Breath Weapon, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), flight, [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17), or immunity to sleep. The ability functions as it did for the original creature, except it uses your class DC or your spell DC (whichever is higher) instead of the creature’s DC. The mutagen grants only abilities based on a creature’s physiology and never grants magic-related abilities such as innate spells or spellcasting ability. The GM ultimately decides what ability a transmogrifying mutagen grants.

Unlike normal for mutagens and [](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effects, you can drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens and gain benefits from each. When you drink transmogrifying mutagens made from different creatures, you receive abilities from each creature. When you drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens made from the same type of creature, such as multiple mutagens made from trolls, you gain an additional ability for each transmogrifying mutagen you drink, and the duration of the abilities from that creature type increases by 1 hour for each additional concoction you drink.

 However, these additional benefits come with a risk; if you drink a transmogrifying mutagen while at least one other is active, after drinking it, you must succeed at a flat check with a DC equal to the total number of active transmogrifying mutagens you’ve consumed. On a failure, you fully transform into a member of the species of the latest transmogrifying mutagen you drank, and you almost always go berserk from your change. The transformation may leave some amount of your personality and memories intact, at the GM’s discretion.

**Destruction** Simultaneously feeding the philosopher’s extractor sizable portions of an aeon, angel, archon, azata, daemon, demon, devil, protean, and psychopomp, each of at least 14th level, along with a philosopher’s stone causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 254 <sup>2.0</sup>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wide, single-use mask is designed to be slipped over your mouth and nose and its alchemical filter activated all with one hand. Once activated, the mask sharpens odors, giving you [imprecise scent](/Rules.aspx?ID=417) with the listed range. You can't wear other masks while you're wearing a bloodhound mask. When you use [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) a creature by its scent, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level even if you're untrained, and the mask grants you the listed item bonus to your Survival check. The GM sets the Survival DC based on the area's ability to hold scent rather than on visual clues, as normal for using scent.

This sticky salve stubbornly holds wounds closed and encourages swift natural healing. You can activate the salve in either of the following ways.

If you roll a success on the Medicine check, you get a critical success instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vestige Lenses](/Equipment.aspx?ID=767)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 25

**Price** 40 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These simple lenses are alchemically treated to detect the faint smoke trail from a piece of specially formulated sandalwood incense. This incense has an odor undetectable by most people and a long burn time, making it perfect for discreetly tracking individuals. A stick of this incense costs 1 sp and can safely burn for up to 8 hours. While wearing the lenses, you see alchemical fumes in a distinct green tint, granting you a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) a creature marked with the incense and to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) any alchemical vapors. If the smoke is fresh, Tracking via the incense's fumes might use a lower DC than normal for tracking a creature walking on firm surfaces.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Vestige Lenses

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=116" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 86

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gummy liquid disproportionately lengthens your legs, causing you to grow but making your movement awkward. The effect is very noticeable unless your clothes can adequately conceal it.

 **Benefit** You gain an item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and you gain the listed status bonus to your Speed. In addition, you grow one size larger, but your larger size does not have any additional effects beyond the potential change in space.

 **Drawback** You take a –1 penalty to AC and a –2 penalty to Reflex saves.

</column>

This [caligni](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=18)-made, murky-green drug supercharges a creature's olfactory senses at the expense of dulling their mind. Popular throughout the Darklands for its ability to transform normally dull scents and flavors into intense, euphoric experiences, grolna can also be a great aid to trackers who want to follow scent trails, turning ordinary humanoids into effective bloodhounds.

---

A patchwork of humanoid flesh makes up this grotesque mask stitched together with black silk or wire. It is distinctive for its bulbous orange eye— crafted from a magical glass bauble—and wide row of teeth. When worn, the mask amplifies your ability to sense fear in other creatures. You automatically know the value of the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition of any [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27) creature, and you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) frightened creatures. Whenever you deal precision damage to a frightened creature, you deal 1 additional precision damage. If you are not evil, you are [drained 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) while wearing the _Skinsaw mask_.

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Players can gain access to faction-specific gear by taking the corresponding Faction Gear Access Game Reward, available when they reach 20 reputation with the respective faction._

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

**Access** Membership in the Envoy's Alliance Pathfinder Society faction.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A typical Pathfinder writ of authenticity confirms the holder's status as a member of the Pathfinder Society and their intended business. Most writs are pieces of fine parchment folded, bound with gold cord, and sealed with three wax seals. The top seal is always the Glyph of the Open Road and the middle one is the Envoy's Alliance open door emblem. The bottom seal uses the preparer's personal sigil. Inside, the text describes a specific instance of a legitimate business activity, with blanks for the Pathfinder to fill in and personalize the writ to the persons and activity desired. Presenting a writ of authenticity grants a +2 item bonus to [Make a Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) for the associated business, assuming the writ is legitimate and the viewer expects to work with the Pathfinder Society for that activity.

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). [Playing Cards](/Equipment.aspx?ID=873)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A standard deck of cards consists of 54 cards made from thick paper contained within a paper sleeve. The most common deck used for games and gambling is known as the Old Mage deck and features four suits themed with the four essences of magic, each with 13 cards, as well as two wildcards. The name and appearance of the deck varies from region to region, such as the Magician's Deck in Taldor or the Deck of Masks in the Shackles.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Marked Playing Cards
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

</row>

</column>

---

A deck of marked playing cards appears to be an ordinary deck upon initial inspection but bears specific folds, colors, scratches, or other markings on each card that allow an informed user to know what's on the other side of a card. A deck of marked cards grants you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks or other relevant checks to gamble with the cards. You can determine that an unattended deck of cards is marked with a successful DC 20 Perception check. Determining that a deck is marked during play is more difficult and is typically determined by a Perception check against the dealer's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC.

[Rubbing Set](/Equipment.aspx?ID=874)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

By using a rubbing set, you can quickly make a copy of carvings or etchings you find during your explorations, making them easier to accurately reproduce. This kit consists of a roll of thin onion-skin paper in a waterproof leather case, several thick wax crayons, and a bar of sealing wax that can be melted and used to temporarily hold the paper in place while you take the rubbing. Using the kit consumes the materials and provides a +1 item bonus on checks to document or reproduce artwork or writing that has been carved, etched, or otherwise physically added to a surface.

These folding, wood-framed spectacles hold flat discs of cut crystal as lenses and are held in place with thin cords that wrap around each ear, with another strap holding them around the neck while not in use. While you are wearing the spectacles, you gain a +1 item bonus to checks to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Unfolding the spectacles onto the bridge of the nose, you gain the effects of 2nd-level [_comprehend language_](/Spells.aspx?ID=46) for one hour except that it applies to all languages you see rather than a single language, and it does not apply to language you hear.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Sun Wheel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=905)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Otari</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Otari](/Sources.aspx?ID=55) pg. 60

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Created by the priests of a Qadiran sect of [Sarenites](/Deities.aspx?ID=16), the _sun wheels_ were designed to protect the Dawnflower's followers in their quest to hunt down a dangerous cult trying to raise a spawn of the evil god [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=15). Once they completed their crusade, these priests disbanded and went on to minister other congregations. They each took their _sun wheels_ with them, handing them down to the next generations.

 This copper medallion is etched with a stylized sun, its rays shaped like the spokes of a wagon wheel. It tends to glint brightly when exposed to sunlight. While wearing this pendant, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks. You must be good-aligned to use the sun wheel's true power: the following activation, which provides you a shield of burning force.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> concentrate;     **Effect** The _sun wheel_ casts a [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=280) spell benefiting you. When you use the spell to prevent damage, you prevent 10 damage instead of 5. If the attacker is adjacent to you, you can choose to deal 2d6 fire damage to it, which it gets a DC 21 basic Reflex save to resist.

 If you choose to deal the fire damage, you can't Activate _the sun wheel_ again until the next morning. If you prevent damage but don't deal the fire damage, you can use it again in 10 minutes, as normal for _shield_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Sun Wheel

[Secret-Keeper's Mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=914)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67)

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Each of these full-face masks is made of stitched materials—often including humanoid skin—and has a single, bulbous eye. While wearing the mask, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) and the mask doesn't impair your vision. The mask can also be activated, with an ability based on its type.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs=""
>
Secret-Keeper's Mask (Blackfingers)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67) pg. 0

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This featureless mask is made of thin, papery skin. Its single eye is a fragile bubble of venom-filled glass.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twist the mask's eye and peer at an object. You know whether the object is poison or has been poisoned, but you don't learn the number or type of poisons present in the object.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 5"
pfs=""
>
Secret-Keeper's Mask (Gray Master)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67) pg. 0

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This monochrome mask is made of tattered rags of gray and black cloth and bleached fragments of skin.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You succeed on a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) an item of negligible Bulk;  **Effect** You create an illusory duplicate of the item you just stole. This duplicate has the appropriate appearance and weight, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. The illusion vanishes after 10 minutes, or earlier if anyone examines or manipulates the illusory duplicate (such as to try to use it).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 6"
pfs=""
>
Secret-Keeper's Mask (Father Skinsaw)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67) pg. 0

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This mask is a patchwork of tanned skins, each with a distinctive scar. It is contorted into a caricature of a face with a leering eye.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You deal [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) to a creature;  **Effect** The bleeding wound you cause is particularly mutilating. The DC of flat checks to recover from the persistent bleed damage is increased by 2, and the target creature has a –2 status penalty to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while it is bleeding and for 1 minute after it ceases bleeding.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs=""
>
Secret-Keeper's Mask (Reaper of Reputation)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67) pg. 0

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This mask is made of gray and black tiles sewn together. It has a messy, inky spiral over the mouth.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact (auditory, linguistic);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch the mask's spiral and identify a target creature within 30 feet. For the next 10 minutes, any normal speech you utter can, at your discretion, be inaudible to all creatures except the target creature, who can hear you clearly regardless of ambient sound so long as it is within 1 mile. This ability doesn't silence magical words, such as the verbal component of spellcasting or commands to activate magic items.
name: Secret-Keeper's Mask (Blackfingers)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM's Toolkit: Secret Keeper's Mask](/Sources.aspx?ID=67)

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Each of these full-face masks is made of stitched materials—often including humanoid skin—and has a single, bulbous eye. While wearing the mask, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) and the mask doesn't impair your vision. The mask can also be activated, with an ability based on its type.

<row gap="medium">

This featureless mask is made of thin, papery skin. Its single eye is a fragile bubble of venom-filled glass.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twist the mask's eye and peer at an object. You know whether the object is poison or has been poisoned, but you don't learn the number or type of poisons present in the object.

---

This cloth of gold cape was originally gifted to one of Goka's emperors centuries ago. Since then, it has spawned many imitations, which are all alike in that they are dyed with an elaborate seal depicting two drakes flanking Goka's palace and the Seven Dragons Bridge. The beautiful cape grants you a +3 item bonus to checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) and to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50). While you wear the cape, the weather (including wind and fog) doesn't affect your movement or vision. Additionally, whenever you fall while wearing the _cape of the open sky_, the cape automatically casts [_feather fall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=111) on you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** The cape becomes a pair of golden drake wings that grant you a fly Speed of 30 feet for 1 hour.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The cloak pushes you onward. You Stride or [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to your Speed, but you can move only in a straight line. You gain a +15-foot status bonus to your Speed and fly Speed for this movement.

markdown:
May contain spoilers from Malevolence **Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 67 **Price** 650 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Even during the time of Thassilon, when the Order of the Starless Night still existed, _starless scopes_ were uncommon. Today, this final scope might well be the last one to survive the passage of time. A _starless scope_ is a handheld telescope crafted of silver and fine wood. When one peers at the sky through a _starless scope_, one always views the sky as if during a clear night. A starless scope adds a +2 item bonus to [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and Perception checks made to observe the skies, as it causes all celestial objects to dim when not directly observed, allowing its user to more easily observe their intended subject. It also grants a +2 item bonus to all [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks made to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24). A starless scope also functions as a divine focus for worshipers of [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=5). The magic of a starless scope requires a specially prepared lens to function, and it's possible to shatter the lens if you roll poorly when activating the _starless scope_. Without a functional lens, a _starless scope_ doesn't function. You can replace a shattered lens with a functional lens by taking a two-action activity with the manipulate trait. If you know the formula for the starless scope, you can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) a new lens with a DC 25 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) (master) check. A starless scope lens is a level 9 item worth 100 gp. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** you use the _starless scope_ as a divine focus; **Requirements** you worship Desna; **Effect** You attempt to enhance the effects of a spell as you cast it by attempting a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check against the spell's DC, as determined by [Table 10–5](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) **Critical Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +2 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –2 status penalty. If you would normally cast the spell from a spell slot, and the spell is 5th level or lower, you don't spend the spell slot and cast the spell from the _starless scope_ instead.
**Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +1 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –1 status penalty.
**Failure** The spell is cast normally. Attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Critical Failure** The spell is disrupted and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters. **Activate** Interact ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You raise the scope to your eye and observe a creature within 30 feet. You can attempt to identify the creature by [Recalling Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The _starless scope_ adds a +2 item bonus to this check. If the creature is associated with the Dominion of the Black or the Elder Mythos, or is a creature whose actions have blasphemed against Desna (Ioseff Xarwin's ghost falls into this latter category), the creature must attempt a DC 27 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected, and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Success** The creature shines with starlight for 1 round. During this time, the creature can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) if it is visible. If it's [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's concealed rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). item_bonus_note: Astronomy Lore checks made while using the mirror
markdown:
May contain spoilers from Malevolence **Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 68 **Usage** mounted in frame (see below) **Bulk** 3 --- The _Void Mirror_ was created on a distant planet by a now-extinct alien cult to aid in unlocking the secrets of the Dark Tapestry. It appears as a 5-foot-tall, 2-foot-wide mirror of dark glass. As long as it's unmounted in a frame, the _Void Mirror_ functions only as a mirror, save that it always reflects the sky as if it were night, regardless of the time of day. When the _Void Mirror_ is mounted in a frame, it instead serves as a window into space, displaying a star field in its glass rather than a reflection. This frame can be of any quality, but stouter frames help to prevent the frame's destruction and thus help to keep the _Void Mirror_ functional. The view presented by the _Void Mirror_ is any view of the night sky possible from its current physical location, regardless of time of day. Observations of the sky in this way add a +3 item bonus to [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Perception checks made while using the mirror. The point of view can be shifted through hand gestures, causing the scene within the mirror to reorient in any direction desired. A character who peers into the starscape within the _Void Mirror_ must attempt a DC 41 Will save. On a failure, the character feels something looking back at them from the dark places between the stars. On a critical failure, this sensation causes the character to become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19). The character is then temporarily immune to this effect for 24 hours. By placing the _Void Mirror_ in a specially-constructed frame (such as the one within the Cosmic Crypt in this adventure), it can halt the ongoing transformation of a creature that has performed the apotheosis activation. Building such a frame is beyond the skill of low-level characters, as it requires an artisan with legendary proficiency in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4). The _Void Mirror_ can be utilized in other ways, but before a character can activate these effects the occult methods to access these ritual-like effects must be [Researched](/Rules.aspx?ID=1205) separately. Since the specific methods for these activations vary slightly from person to person, these methods can't be taught; each person who seeks to activate the _Void Mirror_ in one of the following ways must complete their own research to unlock the artifact's secrets. Each requires a separate number of [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks to Research, as detailed below for each activation. **Activate** 1 hour (Intract); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 20 Occultism (expert) checks when Researching (1 week per attempt); **Frequency** once per month; **Effect** The first activation ritual is known as “Speak to the Void” and allows the user to contact an intelligence in a distant part of the universe, provided the mirror shows that location (regardless of distance). This alien intelligence infuses the user's mind with answers, allowing the user to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) using [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=22) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) as if they were legendary proficiency with the skill (including the +8 proficiency bonus). If this check fails, the character takes 10d6 mental damage (100 mental damage on a critical failure) as the imparted knowledge does more harm than good. **Activate** 1 hour (Interact); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 30 Occultism (master) checks when Researching (1 month per attempt); **Frequency** once per year; **Effect** The second activation ritual is known as “Call from the Void.” The user performs a 1-hour-long rite before the _Void Mirror_, during which they indicate a type of [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=77), [ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=122), or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) creature that's an alien life form from the planet the user is currently located on. The target creature must be a level equal to or less than the user's level +4. As the rite ends, the user attempts an Occultism check against the target creature's Will DC. **Critical Success** The creature is drawn across the universe to appear in a space adjacent to the _Void Mirror_. The creature's initial attitude toward the user is [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21), but this attitude can shift quickly if the creature realizes its goals and personality differs dramatically from the user's, or if the user makes a request of the creature that's against its nature. As long both the creature and the user are within 30 feet of the _Void Mirror_, the user can return the creature to its original location by Dismissing this activation. The creature can attempt a Will save against the user's Occultism DC to resist being returned; if it succeeds, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** As critical success, but the creature is [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25) upon arrival.
**Failure** As critical success, but the creature is [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) upon arrival.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but magical feedback from the failed activation causes the user to become [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). **Activate** 7 days (Interact); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 40 Occultism (legendary) checks when Researching (1 year per attempt); **Frequency** once per century; **Effect** The third activation ritual is known as “Become the Void” and requires the user to continue performing the rite for 7 consecutive days (as if they were performing a multi-day ritual). If the user fails to perform this rite for one of these 7 consecutive days, they immediately suffer the critical failure effect below. **Critical Success** The user's body, mind, and soul are infused with alien energies drawn from the Dark Tapestry, which transforms the user into an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) of a level no higher than their current level +4. This new form could be an existing aberration or a unique one of the GM's creation. The user retains their memories and spellcasting ability (including any rituals they know) but becomes chaotic evil and loses all other abilities they possessed in their previous form.
**Success** As critical success, but the aberration the user transforms into can be of a level no higher than half the user's current level.
**Failure** The user's attempt to change is a painful mistake that deals 10d6+40 bludgeoning damage as their body twists, bends and breaks. Ultimately, they are not transformed.
**Critical Failure** The user is slain, but their body shifts and transforms into a brand new creature as the bodiless alien intelligence Tchekuth incubates within the user's flesh, mind and soul. This transformation takes another 7 days to complete but can be halted indefinitely if the _Void Mirror_ is placed in a specially constructed frame aimed at the body's location (regardless of any solid object between the mirror and the body). Slowing or stopping this transformation via other means requires complex rituals or divine intervention, subject to the GM's whim. After 7 days, the body completes its transformation and Tchekuth rises once more as a physical threat. **Destruction** A creature that completes the apotheosis of Becoming the Void can destroy the _Void Mirror_ by smashing it, though doing so also destroys the creature performing this action in a violent burst of occult energy
